message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on phenotype alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; PGS000753 is prevalent AAA but still aligned). Among disease-focused candidates, the Nat Genet multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis models (PGS003972/PGS003973) are preferred over pan-trait/framework-style scores (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability framework) and over the older sparse P+T prevalent model (PGS000753), consistent with the domain policy favoring disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analyses for large-vessel diseases. Between the Nat Genet siblings, PGS003972 has a full-model AUROC=0.69 with covariates/covariate set unknown, while PGS003973 reports a high C-index=0.882 but with age/sex covariates and no PRS-only or covariates-regressed-out metric; given the explicit guidance not to treat full-model discrimination as PRS-comparable and the risk that the higher C-index is largely covariate-driven, the more conservative choice is PGS003972. Remaining limitation: across the set, PRS-only metrics and incremental performance are largely missing (and covariates are unknown for several), so the choice cannot be upgraded to high-quality on the visible evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype alignment to abdominal aortic aneurysm (PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent AAA; the others are AAA case definitions without stated restriction). Two candidates (PGS003972, PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance prefers over pan-trait/framework or portability-style scores (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability). Between the Nat Genet siblings, PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but only with basic covariates and without PRS-only/incremental metrics, making it hard to interpret as PRS contribution; PGS003972 provides a more conservative full-model AUROC (0.69) over a similar endpoint and similarly unknown PRS-only metrics. Given the heritability context (h2_liability≈0.02) and the guidance to avoid letting a single full-model discrimination figure dominate when PRS-only metrics are missing, PGS003972 is selected as the best-supported disease-focused direct-match option, but confidence is limited because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC) are largely absent across candidates and covariates are unknown for several models."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance suggests should generally outrank pan-trait/portability framework scores (PGS001784, PGS002054) and an older sparse P+T prevalent model (PGS000753) when endpoints are similarly aligned. Between the Nat Genet siblings, PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) with basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) but lacks PRS-only / covariates-regressed-out metrics; PGS003972 reports a lower full-model AUROC (0.69) and also lacks PRS-only metrics. Because full-model discrimination is not directly comparable to PRS contribution, the apparent superiority of PGS003973 cannot be confidently attributed to the PRS itself; selecting the disease-focused meta-analysis family is best-supported, but choosing between the siblings remains ambiguous. I select PGS003972 as the preferred direct disease-focused meta-analysis PRS without relying on a potentially covariate-driven full-model metric outlier, but confidence is limited by missing PRS-only performance and unclear comparability across the sibling records."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA; one is explicitly prevalent). Among the most disease-focused candidates, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from the same dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with large multi-cohort development, which domain guidance favors over framework/portability scores (PGS001784: Global Biobank PRS-CS-auto; PGS002054: UKB portability LDpred2). PGS003972 is selected because it provides a more standard AUROC metric without additional covariate complexity disclosed, but the absence of PRS-only/incremental metrics and ambiguity around metric comparability across candidates keeps the overall recommendation sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection hinges on study archetype + comparable performance evidence. PGS003972 (PRS-CS; Nat Genet 2023 GWAS meta-analysis) is disease-focused, multi-cohort (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) and avoids the two main framework-style alternatives: the UKB portability sweep (PGS002054) and the Global Biobank pan-trait analyses paper (PGS001784), which domain policy says should not beat disease-focused scores based mainly on metric availability/validation size. Among the disease-focused options, PGS003972 reports only a moderate full-model AUROC (0.69) but that metric is not PRS-only; however it provides a coherent, externally oriented evidence package. PGS000753 is older, sparse (29 variants), and explicitly prevalent AAA (domain policy for cardiovascular/large-vessel diseases favors newer disease-focused meta-analysis models over older prevalent sparse models). PGS003973 is a sibling from the same Nat Genet study with a much higher C-index (0.882), but that appears to be a full-model metric with basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) and lacks PRS-only/PGS-only performance; its apparent advantage may be largely covariate-driven and is not directly comparable to PRS discrimination, so it is not enough to outweigh the broader disease-focused meta-analysis support without additional PRS-only metrics. Confidence is limited because across the top contenders the reported metrics are mostly full-model (or partial-r), PRS-only AUROC is absent, and covariates are unknown for some models, making cross-model comparability imperfect."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (“abdominal aortic aneurysm”), so selection hinges on study archetype, comparability of performance evidence, and covariate cleanliness. PGS000753 comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and provides a clear per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) in a sizable EUR validation (n=46,564), aligning with the domain guidance to prefer disease-focused models over framework/portability sweeps when endpoints are similar. Competing models either come from framework/portability-style efforts (PGS001784 ‘Global Biobank…’; PGS002054 ‘Portability of 245…’) or report only full-model discrimination without PRS-only isolation and/or unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973). PGS003973’s high C-index (0.882) is not PRS-only and is therefore not directly comparable; similarly, PGS001784’s AUROC=0.868 is full-model and its PGS-only R2 is small (0.0147), so the apparent advantage could be covariate-driven. Overall confidence is limited because several candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and covariate details, making cross-model performance comparability weak despite clear phenotype alignment."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo align to abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is AAA for all, with PGS000753 explicitly prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS003972, PGS003973) come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance favors over pan-trait/portability framework scores (PGS001784 Cell Genomics; PGS002054 AJHG portability) and over screening/cost-effectiveness framing (PGS003429 Nat Commun). Between the Nat Genet siblings, the metadata provide no PRS-only AUROC/R2; PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but that is not directly comparable PRS evidence and could be covariate-driven (it includes age/sex), whereas PGS003972 reports a more modest full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates; given the emphasis on avoiding over-weighting a single full-model metric and preferring coherent disease-focused evidence, I select PGS003972 as the cleaner default from the disease-focused family. Limitation: lack of PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUC) and unclear covariates for PGS003972 keep confidence below high and make the choice sensitive to unobserved validation-record details."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and (mostly) phenotyping_reported. Two models are from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis in Nat Genet (PGS003972/PGS003973), which domain guidance favors over pan-trait/portability frameworks when endpoint fidelity is similar. Between those siblings, PGS003972 has a full-model AUROC of 0.69 in EUR (n=6,940) with covariates unknown; PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index 0.882 (EUR, n=7,517) but with age/sex covariates, and there is no PRS-only/incremental metric shown for either—so the large C-index is likely heavily covariate-driven and not directly comparable as PRS evidence. Other competitors include framework/portability-style scores (PGS001784, PGS002054) with modest PRS-only/partial-r (~0.014–0.0147) and one older sparse P+T model (PGS000753, OR=1.37). Given missing PRS-only metrics for the disease-focused Nat Genet scores and non-comparability of full-model AUROC/C-index across covariate sets, the selection of PGS003972 over PGS003973 and the framework scores remains uncertain, hence low confidence and a sub-optimal direct-match outcome."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004561","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS004491, PGS004561), both aligned to acute kidney injury via EFO and identical endpoint labeling in phenotyping_reported/trait_reported (N17 acute renal failure), with the same publication, training cohort (UKB), training sample size (n=174,489), evaluation ancestry (EUR), validation size (n=56,192), and identical variant count.
